threatFindings.threat: [4A17h] hook-cell race vs V6-family opponents: base B writes [4A17h] at instruction 3, exactly like V6/V4/V6Guard, so execution order decides who receives zombies captured through jmp [4A17h] (zom20a via A's patch, b/d via B's patch).
threatFindings.evidence: Static: dis86 of rev0 B and refs V6/V4/V6Guard B (mov [4A17h],bx at offset 8, instruction 3 in all). Moving our write to instruction 6 (C1): threat 20261003183104832-A003-threat-19llx copies 2 ALL +0.0142 [0.0000,0.0284]; 20261003184906991-A003-threat-5hja6 copies 3 ALL +0.0151 [-0.0149,0.0451]; screen V6-family cohorts about +0.003 on average.
threatFindings.impact: Small: roughly +0.015 to +0.02 per battle in V6-family-heavy fields, near zero elsewhere. Captured zombies do not score; the gain is denial of the opponent's zombies only.

threatFindings.threat: Losing the zom20a INT87 race to other 2025 capturers (AVI_Fishandpoultry2 and HDS_YOY2 replace 41 93 E2 F2 with FF 26 <own cell>).
threatFindings.evidence: Static: Fishandpoultry2 runs INT87 at its instruction 15, HDS_YOY2 at instruction 22; base A at instruction 10 (C1: 8). Base already patches first, and after our patch the live bytes 41 93 FF 26 no longer match their pattern. Same-pattern V6-family A's tie on INT87, but they write identical bytes, so only the cell race matters. Moving INT87 earlier gives no benefit; moving it later than instruction 15 would lose this race in cohorts with Fishandpoultry/YOY.

threatFindings.threat: zom20a mimic decoys: A's forward search from DI=0 patches the first E2 F2 81 C3, which may be dead decoy code in HRZ_Grindo_Holics1 (offset 33h, behind jmp 56h), Grindo_Holics2 (45h, 1C5h) or GSA_callfart1/2 (46h / 4h) when those load below zom20a.
threatFindings.evidence: Static byte scan (agent2/night/scratch/A003/scan.mjs). Timing cannot help: the decoys sit in the carriers' load images and persist. zomb_Grindo threat cohorts gave exactly 0 difference for C1 (20261003183104832-A003-threat-19llx), so INT87 timing does not interact with this threat. Fix belongs to a search-start or pattern change (card A038).

threatFindings.threat: Theft of the [9769h] (Registered_Winners) and [5D13h] (m050/b01d) hook cells through write timing.
threatFindings.evidence: Static: Registered_Winners1 writes [9769h] at instruction 3 (base A copies at instruction 5, C1 at 10, both later, so we keep the cell); ChimeraA/b01dA write [5D13h] at instruction 3-4, base and C1 B at instruction 5. No field opponent writes these cells later.
threatFindings.impact: None found; C1 keeps both cells after their competitors' writes.

recommendation: Do not promote on this evidence alone. C1 is a zero-byte-cost reordering: screen ALL +0.0046 [-0.0026,0.0119] (below the +0.006 bar, no group clearly negative), with a consistent but small V6-family gain in two threat jobs (+0.014 and +0.015). Treat it as a free low-risk add-on: include it in a combination screen with any other promoted change. Moving zom20a's INT87 earlier or later on its own has no lever: base A already wins the INT87 race against every 2025 zom20a capturer.
notes: Card A003: INT87 timing. Static analysis shows the zom20a INT87 race is already won (A at instruction 10, competitors at 15 and 22). The only real race is the [4A17h] cell race against V6-family opponents, which A's reorder makes possible: A must read [4A17h] after B's later write. A 'later INT87' variant was not run: by static analysis it can only lose (to Fishandpoultry2 if past instruction 15). Screen outcomes are identical in 30 of 50 cohorts; the rest are chaotic divergences of 1-3 battles.
